resources.string: Enter the address of the dashboard your Hermes host runs (hermes dashboard, port 9119 by default), or scan the code Hermes shows you.
Only needed when the dashboard is behind Cloudflare Access. Sent only over HTTPS, and only to this dashboard.
This address only works on the computer running Hermes, not from a phone. Ask Hermes for its Tailscale or network address instead.
Stored encrypted on this phone, never in backups. Lets the app sign in again when the session expires.
Point the camera at the QR code Hermes showed you.
That code is not a Hermes dashboard address or sign-in link.
The camera is needed to scan the code. You can type the address instead.
This device has no camera available.
%1$s and its saved sign-in will be removed from this phone. Nothing changes on the Hermes host.
This dashboard signs you in on its own page. It opens in your browser, and you come back here when you are signed in.
Finish signing in in the browser…
Extra headers for a reverse proxy
Sent with every request to this server over HTTPS, for a proxy in front of Hermes that asks for them. The values are kept encrypted on this phone.
This isn\'t a valid header name. Use letters, digits and dashes.
The app manages this header itself, so it can\'t be set here.
Header values can\'t contain line breaks.
This header is already in the list.
Extra headers are only sent over HTTPS. Enter an https:// address first.
Unlock with fingerprint, face or screen lock
Each time the app starts, this dashboard opens after you unlock. Its saved sign-in stays on this phone either way.
This app connects to a Hermes dashboard you (or your assistant) run yourself. The dashboard has to be up before the app can reach it.
Do you have your Hermes dashboard login credentials?
This means the Hermes dashboard username and password you sign in with, not Tailscale, Cloudflare or Google credentials.
How will this phone reach Hermes?
Pick how the app should reach your self-hosted Hermes dashboard. You can change this later.
Use or edit current dashboard address
I\'m on the same network as Hermes
Use this when this phone and the Hermes machine are on the same home or local network.
Use Tailscale when you want to reach Hermes securely while away from home.
I already have a domain or reverse proxy
Use this if you already reach Hermes through an HTTPS hostname you manage.
Using the app at home, on the same network as the Hermes machine? Choose “I\'m on the same network as Hermes”.
Need access away from home without existing remote access? Choose Tailscale, the simplest secure option.
Already running an HTTPS domain or reverse proxy for Hermes? Choose “I already have a domain or reverse proxy”.
Here is what you need to connect over your local network:
You can sign in to the Hermes dashboard.
You know the Hermes machine\'s local IP address.
This phone is on the same reachable network.
Tailscale gives you secure access from anywhere, including the recommended Tailscale Serve path:
Tailscale is installed on the Hermes machine.
Tailscale is installed on this phone.
Both are signed in to the same tailnet.
Hermes configures Tailscale Serve for the dashboard.
Hermes tells you the address to enter here.
The app never installs or configures Tailscale, and it doesn\'t assume an address or port. Hermes tells you what to use.
This is only for HTTPS infrastructure you already run. The app doesn\'t guide you through creating one.
Your existing HTTPS Hermes dashboard address, for example https://hermes.example.com, https://hermes.example.com:9443 or https://example.com/hermes.
Any path prefix your proxy uses.
A way to sign in to the dashboard.
The app will not ask you to expose a raw public port, create firewall rules or bypass certificate checks.
Ask Hermes to set up the dashboard
Please set up or start the Hermes dashboard for me. Make sure it requires authentication, and tell me which port it is using when it is ready. Do not disable authentication.
Ask Hermes to check the dashboard
Please check whether the Hermes dashboard is currently running. If it is, tell me which port it uses. If it is not running, set it up or start it. Make sure dashboard authentication remains enabled.
Ask Hermes to set up dashboard credentials

Please check the authentication configuration for my Hermes dashboard. If dashboard login credentials have not been configured yet, set them up securely and tell me what username and password I should use with the Hermes app on my Android phone. Do not disable authentication.
Ask Hermes to check your dashboard sign-in

Does my Hermes dashboard require authentication? If so, tell me what username and password I should use with the Hermes app on my Android phone. If authentication is not configured, set it up securely. Do not disable authentication.
Ask Hermes for your connection details

Please make sure the Hermes dashboard is reachable from other devices on my local network, then tell me the machine\'s local IP address and the dashboard port I should use with the Hermes app on my Android phone. Keep dashboard authentication enabled.
Ask Hermes to configure Tailscale Serve

Please check whether the Hermes dashboard is running. Make sure Tailscale is available on this machine, then configure Tailscale Serve so I can securely reach the dashboard from my Android phone. Keep dashboard authentication enabled. When it is ready, tell me the hostname or address and port I should use with the Hermes app.
Ask Hermes to confirm your HTTPS address

Please confirm the HTTPS URL I should use to reach the Hermes dashboard through my existing reverse proxy, including any custom port or path prefix. Also confirm that dashboard authentication remains enabled.
Choose the scheme Hermes gave you
A Tailscale Serve name (.ts.net) always uses HTTPS.
Choose how this phone will reach Hermes.
Enter a valid host or IP address.
Enter the full HTTPS dashboard address.
Choose HTTP or HTTPS to match the address Hermes supplied.
Enter your Hermes dashboard username and password.
These are your Hermes dashboard username and password, not your Tailscale, Cloudflare or Google account.
The app checks the server, the dashboard and the sign-in. Nothing is saved until you sign in.
This dashboard uses username and password sign-in. Enter your credentials to finish testing the connection.
This connection is ready to use.
This dashboard uses browser-based sign-in. The sign-in screen opens it after you use these settings.
This dashboard offers more than one way to sign in. Choose one on the sign-in screen, or enter your username and password to test them now.
Checks for HTTPS and certificate problems when connecting to your dashboard.

If you use your own certificate authority, install its certificate on this phone as a CA certificate (in Android\'s settings, search for “CA certificate”). The app trusts the authorities Android trusts and those you install; Tailscale Serve and Let\'s Encrypt certificates need nothing installed.
Check the server certificate\'s expiration and validity dates.
Confirm this phone\'s date and time are correct.
Checks for Cloudflare Access service-token problems when connecting to your dashboard.
Verify the Client ID and Secret belong to a Cloudflare Access service token for this application.
Make sure a Service Auth policy allows that token to reach this Access application.
Or leave the Cloudflare Access fields empty to sign in through the browser instead.
You can leave both empty to test the connection without signing in.
Another saved dashboard already uses that address. Nothing was changed.
The live connection didn\'t open. The address was put back; test the connection again.
This dashboard uses browser-based sign-in. Sign in now to reconnect to it.
This dashboard offers more than one way to sign in. Sign in now to reconnect, or enter your username and password to test them first.
This dashboard has a sign-in service in front of it. Its sign-in page opens here in the app; once you are signed in, you come straight back.
